title: Roamless eSIM NO expiry great for travel
body:
O.P.
this post was edited
There are so many travel eSIMs out there, and I've tried many. But this is a great "set and forget" option for most travellers who need only a few GB of data for a trip, with the one global eSIM able to roam in 165 countries without expiry. https://roamless.com/
Pros – 1. NO expiry of data, and eSIM only needs to be installed once 2. simple USD amount in account that can be used for roaming in all covered countries, no need to get new or different eSIMs or plan each time you need to use. 3. Very reasonable rates in Europe (USD2.45 per GB of data) and USA (USD3.25 per GB of data) for low volume travel data users, and just top up with USD 5 minimum whenever you need. More expensive in Asia but now works in many Asian countries – Japan USD5.95/GB, Singapore USD8.95/GB
Cons – Beware of much higher roaming rates in some countries – eg Qatar USD 15.71 per GB. So check the cost for the countries you are visiting.
Have used in Europe and Singapore, no problems. Plan to use in forthcoming trips to China, Japan and Singapore.
For me, the greatest advantage is that the funds don't expire and the eSIM once installed is always available and can be turned on and off whenever needed, so can just top up account on app with USD5 as needed for travel throughout the world.

[User #1593421573 postsPencilmanLoving NBN on HFC! Yes,really!Whirlpool Enthusiast] O.P.
Just a heads up on Roamless.
I recommended this to some visitors to Australia – turned out to be a bit of disaster initially. They tested Roamless in their home country – all working fine. Then when they landed in Australia, Roamless didn't work!!! The Roamless SIM just didn't seem to want to connect..... So they had to pay roaming charges on their home SIM to catch an Uber etc.
They got on to Roamless help via the app later that day – to Roamless' credit, response was quick. Turned out the solution was that they had to manually select the Telstra network. On auto network selection which is the default, the Roamless eSIM was locking on to the Optus network which did not work for Roamless! (although it's supposed to be supported). Once the Telstra network was manually selected – it was OK. All this actually took a couple of hours to sort out, so was very unpleasant.
So the tip is – if Roamless not working, use Manual Network selection to select one of the other Roamless roaming partners in the country you are visiting.

[User #742437057 postsTheDocWhirlpool Forums Addict] joca writes...
how far out can you buy an Esim without activating it.
This is going to depend entirely on the eSim provider. Some activate immediately on purchase. Others only activate when you land in (one of) the covered countries and connect to the network (keeping in mind that Australia might be one of the covered countries for regional/global eSIMs). The only way to know is to read the details from the provider, as it can vary from country to country. eg, I'm currently in South Africa. Looking at Airalo, they states for their SA eSIMs that "The validity period starts when the eSIM connects to a mobile network in its coverage area", so you could install and even enable it in Australia, but the clock only starts ticking when you arrive in SA. However if you look at their Thailand ones it states "The validity period starts as soon as the eSIM is installed on a device, even outside of it's coverage area". Some others are "on purchase", not install.
